races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Capitano Josepi
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Kevin & Lauren Frost with Jack Mitchell aboard, unknown style and going preference, but the yard has live form (1/11 last 14 days) and the absence of form data makes this a genuine dark horse in a race where unexposed types can thrive.

runners_data.name: Del Pearo
runners_data.note: Finished sixth on debut over this trip on Good, showing some ability; a natural hold-up horse whose true closing style is squeezed into a midfield berth here, meaning his finishing run will be shorter than ideal — factor in that compression when assessing his winning chance.

runners_data.name: Extragalactic
runners_data.note: William Haggas debutant with Harry Davies, unknown style, lightly raced flag, but the Haggas yard is formidable and the stable hits at 6/45 in the last 14 days — an unknown quantity who could arrive with far more ability than revealed.

runners_data.name: Pressured
runners_data.note: Ran ninth of nine on debut over this course and distance on Good, which is a significant form concern; fading-in-finish flag and that bare result suggest he needs to show considerable improvement to feature here.

runners_data.name: Strong Performance
runners_data.note: Finished eighth on debut over seven furlongs on Good and carries a fades-in-finish warning; William Knight's yard is ticking over (3/15 last 14 days) but the opening effort gives little confidence he can reverse that debut below-par showing at the same trip.

runners_data.name: Top Cote
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the field, rated just OR 70 and stepping up sharply in class, but with precedent for leading (hg:p) and the uncontested lead entirely to himself; a long layoff of 104 days is the main fitness query, though Yarmouth's flat straight will suit his front-running style perfectly.

runners_data.name: Hidden Beyond
runners_data.note: Ran a promising third on debut over seven furlongs on Standard, and Daniel Muscutt — a strong Yarmouth jockey — takes the ride for Charles Hills; the switch to Good ground after a Standard debut is an unknown, but the course and distance profile suits a horse who already showed ability at this trip.

runners_data.name: Perfect Love
runners_data.note: Eighth on debut over seven furlongs on Standard for Michael Appleby; 40 days between runs and the fades-in-finish note are both concerns, and the step to Good turf adds another unknown after the all-weather debut.

runners_data.name: Mystic Unicorn
runners_data.note: Ran fifth and ninth in both starts on Standard, so the switch to Good turf is genuinely unknown; the horse's natural closing style cannot play to its strengths in this shape because the hold-up population has filled midfield, blunting any late run.

runners_data.name: Rocsane
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form including two seconds over six furlongs on Good is the most relevant raw evidence in the field; OR 69 and a true hold-up horse by nature, but her race position will be midfield rather than rear — that is a smaller disadvantage for her than for the other redistributed horses given she typically comes from a mid-to-rear pitch anyway.

runners_data.name: Theft
runners_data.note: Ran fifth and seventh in both starts at seven and six furlongs including on Good ground — some experience at the trip and going, but neither run suggests a break-out effort is imminent; the George Scott yard has been in decent nick (2/26 last 14 days) and Darragh Keenan is a capable pilot.

races.paceDynamic: Top Cote is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no serious challenger likely to push into the early lead, shapes to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good ground over Yarmouth's straight seven. That controlled gallop will not burn out the field, meaning the race is unlikely to become a pure stamina test and the early advantage should hold longer into the straight than in a genuinely contested pace scenario. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Mystic Unicorn, Del Pearo, and Rocsane are genuine closers who will be pushed into midfield positions they would not naturally seek, compromising their ability to deliver a late punch. On this shape, prominent racers who can track Top Cote at close quarters and pick up off a true but modest gallop hold the clearest tactical advantage, with hold-up horses disadvantaged by a lack of pace to aim at and their redistribution into midfield meaning they will not get the gaps that a strong pace would open.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Top Cote bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but undemanding pace throughout the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: Top Cote controls the race from the front and the peloton travels in a compact group behind, meaning the winner comes from those positioned second or third early enough to pounce in the final two furlongs; prominent/close-tracking types who can quicken off a modest gallop are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slightly too slow and several horses advance early to race in a tight group behind Top Cote, rewarding those who press from off the shoulder.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a cavalry charge from the two-furlong pole with runners who have been cruising just off the leader finding the clearest daylight and superior finishing speed; lightly-raced unknowns with undisclosed ability could emerge here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Flier Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is just fast enough to stretch the field and a horse who has settled in the middle of the pack produces a sustained run from the three-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A competitive middle-section pace opens enough room down the outside for a mid-division runner to reel in the leaders late; Rocsane's proven placed form at six furlongs on Good suggests she has the consistent finishing effort to get involved if the step up to seven suits her better than her mapping implies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If something goes wrong at the head of affairs — Top Cote runs flat or the early tempo collapses — causing a muddled race that opens a late sprint.
scenarios.body: A chaotic, compressed finish would theoretically benefit true hold-up types, but since Del Pearo, Mystic Unicorn, and Rocsane are redistributed out of their natural rear positions, none are set up to deliver a genuine late burst from far back; this scenario is low-probability precisely because the closers are not where they need to be.

watchPoints.text: Top Cote holds the uncontested lead and, if he has returned fit after 104 days off, his ability to control tempo from the front could dictate the entire race — watch whether he travels comfortably in the early furlongs or is allowed to coast at his own pace.

The redistribution of Del Pearo, Mystic Unicorn, and Rocsane into midfield means three genuine closers will be trapped in traffic behind a compact peloton — watch for crowding and interference in the straight as they seek room that may not materialise.

Hidden Beyond's switch from Standard to Good turf is an unknown, but Daniel Muscutt's booking for Charles Hills represents a notable jockey-trainer angle at Yarmouth — watch the market for any confidence move.

Several debutants (Capitano Josepi, Extragalactic) from powerful yards (Frost, Haggas) have zero public form — watch pre-race market support as the only available signal of stable confidence before the off.

Strong Performance and Pressured both carry fades-in-finish flags and ran poorly on debut; if either of them improves markedly in this second start they could be a factor, but the form trajectory at present points away rather than toward the principals.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Exceeding Expectations In Construction Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Adrestia
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner in a race where she can lead without serious pressure; Simon & Ed Crisford have her fit (33 days, tongue-tie and cheekpieces), and her 14/15 Good-ground sim-going record shows she handles conditions, though recent form shows persistent finishing positions in the 6-17 range on 5f Good — stamina of the lead is the key question.

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with an excellent Good-ground 5f profile including a recent win (form: 1 in last 6), trained by Tom Clover who is 2/17 in his 14-day window; 14 days since last run keeps him fresh and he should secure one of the natural prominent slots with Muscutt in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell three-year-old with a recent 5f Good win in her form string and a 10/11 sim-going record; one of three Cowell runners, she should press prominently with Greatrex up and her form trajectory (5-5-1-0-0 recent) is a positive pattern, though a return to form after a blank run (0) needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (style H, headgear p) who won on Good 5f and has course-applicable form; 21/15 on sim-going shows he struggles to translate effort into results consistently, and Jack Mitchell will need a stronger tempo than Adrestia is likely to provide to get him into the race.

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: Another true hold-up performer for Cowell carrying a p headgear flag, with a 5f Good win in recent history; Marco Ghiani rides and 19 days since last run is fine, but his 7/15 sim-going strike rate is the weakest in the field, and he depends on a pace that opens up the race — not the guaranteed shape here.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: William Haggas four-year-old representing a stable that is 6/45 in the 14-day window — a meaningful strike rate; she should get a prominent position behind the leader and her recent Good 5f fourth suggests she is handling fast conditions, making her a pragmatic each-way profile if the pace suits.

runners_data.name: Hypnotised
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Harry Charlton with two recent Good 5f seconds — consistent form at the level — who races from a hold-up position; 15 days since last run, no headgear, and a 4/6 sim-going record shows selective but genuine aptitude; reliant on late gaps appearing which, in this pace shape, is not the most likely outcome.

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: This filly has genuine prominent racing tendencies — Ashley Lewis (3) takes the ride — but with several prominent types in the field she is likely to find herself further back than natural; her best form (1/5f/STA) came on Standard ground, and the 9-day turnaround for a McBride yard running at 0/2 in the 14-day window adds a layer of caution.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Master
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up specialist at heart who has been bumped into a midfield mapping by the field composition — his true nature means he needs traffic to clear and a fast pace to close into, neither of which is assured; Cowell's fourth runner here, 8 days since last run, and a 4/15 sim-going record underlines that conditions only rarely click for him.

races.paceDynamic: Adrestia is the confirmed front-runner here and, critically, is the only horse likely to uncontestedly lead — she can dictate a smooth, sustainable gallop over Yarmouth's straight 5f on Good ground without being harassed. Rocking Ends, Dazzling Haze, and Kinswoman will press prominently behind her, creating a competitive early order but not a flat-out contested pace battle, since none are true tearaway types likely to blast past Adrestia. Seven Questions, Michaela's Boy, and Hypnotised will track from midfield to rear, with Fantasy Master and Elara May likely unable to secure their natural positions given the number of prominent types in this field — Rocking Ends and Dazzling Haze are most likely to actually hold the prominent slots, with Elara May and Fantasy Master pushed further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone leader setting a honest but manageable tempo — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort to the line, making prominent-to-midfield runners the primary beneficiaries over genuine closers who will need the pace to be hot enough to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Prominent Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Adrestia dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent horses settle cleanly behind her, the race is run at a steady-to-fair clip that rewards those racing close to the pace.
scenarios.body: Adrestia sets a rhythm that no one seriously challenges, allowing Rocking Ends and Dazzling Haze to travel comfortably in the slipstream before unleashing their finishing effort in the straight; both have strong Good-ground 5f form and are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves even more modest than expected and Adrestia steals a decisive advantage that none of the hold-up horses can bridge over 5f.
scenarios.body: Adrestia, freed from any real pressure, lopes along and those behind never generate enough momentum to reel her in; on Good Yarmouth ground, a soft-galloping 5f regularly produces a front-runner winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is sharper than it appears and Seven Questions or Michaela's Boy find a clear passage to close powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Robert Cowell's pair both carry headgear (p) and have each won on Good 5f ground, suggesting they possess a sprint finish if conditions allow; however, with pace not guaranteed to be strong enough, this is an against-the-run-of-play scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Congestion
scenarios.trigger: If the early jostling for position among the prominent types produces interference or a false pace, scrambling the race shape entirely and opening the door for a runner from an unorthodox position.
scenarios.body: Elara May and Fantasy Master, both pushed out of their natural positions and carrying STYLE_FIT discounts, would need this kind of scrambled scenario to make an impact; Hypnotised, stepping up slightly in headgear, could also emerge as a surprise beneficiary if the field bunches and sprints late.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Rocking Ends or Dazzling Haze pushes Adrestia for the early lead — if either pressures her before the first furlong, the pace could hike sharply and fundamentally change which profile benefits.

Elara May and Fantasy Master are both racing out of their natural positions; monitor their early stride — if either scrambles for a prominent pitch, it could cause interference and disrupt the racing pattern for Kinswoman and Dazzling Haze.

Robert Cowell runs four horses (Seven Questions, Michaela's Boy, Dazzling Haze, Fantasy Master) — team tactics are possible, and jockeys may be instructed to set a pace that benefits the stable's hold-up runners, artificially inflating tempo.

Yarmouth's straight 5f on Good ground historically rewards those who race up with the pace or just off it; horses that are four lengths or more off the leader at halfway rarely make up the deficit, so Hypnotised and Seven Questions need to be closer than their style suggests.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Constructing Champions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rose Cotton
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front runner, in fair form with two placed efforts over today's 1m2f trip including a win over 10f on similar going 47 days ago; Tom Clover's stable is hitting at 2/17 over 14 days and Jack Mitchell takes the ride — she simply needs to get a clean break and set her own terms.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Has four placed efforts from seven 12f Good-ground starts and brings strong course form, but runs just nine days after last time and wears a visor; Jack Callan will need to extricate him from the rear in a race that may not stretch far enough for a hold-up horse to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Triple Double A
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old steps back up in trip after a run of disappointing efforts at 8-10f, and the prominent style combined with tp headgear could see him bowl along behind Rose Cotton and stay on; however, his six-run form string reads 775786 and his recent Good-ground record (10th and 7th) offers limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's lightly-campaigned four-year-old ran a creditable third over today's course and distance on Good ground in his penultimate start and won over 12f at Yarmouth on Standard — the combination of proven trip-and-track credentials and a prominent style makes him a natural beneficiary of this race shape.

runners_data.name: Moonjid
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's horse was beaten just over a length when fourth over 10f Good last time and has solid form at that trip, stepping up to 12f today; the p headgear is familiar and Mason Paetel claims 3lb, though a true hold-up style means he needs the early pace to be genuine enough to close into.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's runner returns after a lengthy 88-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field and tempers expectations significantly; his best recent effort was a win on Soft and his Good-ground record (7th, 9th, 11th) is uninspiring — the hold-up style is an additional challenge in what looks like a set-paced contest.

runners_data.name: Solanna
runners_data.note: John Butler's seven-year-old is the oldest runner here and arrives in solid recent form — 1st and 2nd at 10f on Good/Standard — with Daniel Muscutt, one of the more experienced jockeys in the field, taking the ride; T14 strike rate of 3/17 is workmanlike, and a prominent style means he should at least be competitive through the race.

runners_data.name: Arundel
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's four-year-old has strong placed form on Good ground over 10-12f but returns after a staggering 351-day layoff, which is an enormous fitness question mark; naturally a hold-up horse, he finds himself mapped closer to the pace than ideal given the configuration of this field — his chance hinges on whether that layoff has left him race-ready, not just racecourse-ready.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's five-year-old wears a tongue tie and has recent form at shorter trips (8f) on Standard — stepping up markedly in both trip and surface genuinely raises questions about suitability today; like Arundel, his natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the field composition, and Silvestre De Sousa will need to find a pragmatic position that suits neither horse nor track.

races.paceDynamic: Rose Cotton is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no horse in this field capable of or likely to seriously dispute the lead, she will stride into an uncontested, comfortable gallop from the outset over Yarmouth's flat 1m2f. The pace she sets will be honest but controlled — she won over 10f on similar ground last time and clearly stays, so she has no incentive to go excessively hard. Triple Double A and Twilight Moon will push forward to sit close behind on the heels of Rose Cotton, creating a compact early order with a small lead group and a bigger pack behind. Man Of Desert and Arundel are genuine hold-up types in terms of natural style but, with the field carrying more come-from-behind horses than the track map can absorb at the back, both have been redistributed into the midfield picture — Rose Cotton and the two legitimate prominent types (Triple Double A, Twilight Moon) are the ones most likely to actually secure their natural positions. The field holds more hold-up types than can all be comfortably housed at the rear, meaning some will race closer than ideal. This race shape — a lone, unhurried front runner setting a sustainable Good-ground tempo with a compressed chasing pack — favours horses racing prominently or close to the pace who can pounce before the line rather than deep closers trying to make up ground late on a flat, fair track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rose Cotton Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Cotton gets a soft lead and the pace stays honest but not punishing, allowing her to dictate every yard.
scenarios.body: Rose Cotton is uncontested early and, racing over a flat track with no bends to slow momentum, simply conserves energy before kicking clear in the final two furlongs; her recent win over 10f on similar ground confirms she handles the conditions and is in form at OR 74.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the hold-up horses struggle to close, leaving Twilight Moon or Triple Double A to strike from just off the lead.
scenarios.body: A slow-ish gallop compresses the field into a tight bunch entering the straight, and the prominent types who have saved ground through the race are best placed to accelerate; Twilight Moon's course form over 12f on Good and Triple Double A's persistent placed form on Good are both assets here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Cotton's early control paradoxically lulls the field into a false rhythm and a well-timed mid-race mover produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Moonjid or Solanna, travelling strongly through the middle stages, finds clear daylight early in the straight and sustains a run that the front-runners cannot repel; Solanna's Good-ground 10f win and Moonjid's recent Good-ground form over the trip both give credence to this shape if the tempo turns out marginally too slow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick and front-runners tie up inside the final furlong, leaving genuine closers to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given that the two true hold-up horses (Arundel, Man Of Desert) are racing out of their natural roles with compromised positions, and neither has the recent form or fresh-off-a-layoff credentials to capitalise on such a scenario; Patrol, fresh off a 9-day turnaround and wearing a visor, is the most plausible deep closer if the race falls apart at the front.

watchPoints.text: Rose Cotton's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest factor in this race — if she jumps cleanly and gets three lengths of daylight in the first furlong, the race is effectively over as a pace contest.

Twilight Moon's course-and-distance form (3rd and 1st at Yarmouth over 12f on Good/Standard) is the strongest pedigree among the prominent types — watch for Ashley Lewis positioning him just off Rose Cotton's heels from early in the race.

Arundel's 351-day absence is the most significant unknown in the field — Ed Dunlop has a good record returning horses fresh, but that is an extreme layoff and his odds should reflect the fitness risk before backers commit.

Solanna and Moonjid both carry claims from hold-up or midfield positions but will need the early tempo to be brisk enough to close — monitor early sectionals to gauge whether Rose Cotton has injected enough pace to set up a proper finish.

Man Of Desert's last five runs are almost entirely at 8f on Standard ground — today's 1m2f Good surface is a meaningful step into the unknown for Chris Dwyer's runner, and punters should treat any market confidence with caution until his course form profile over this trip is established.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Facilities Management Front Runner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with solid recent form including a third in this grade on Good ground; Mason Paetel's 3lb claim is useful, and 33 days off is manageable — the drop back to 6f from a string of 7f runs could sharpen him.

runners_data.name: Sam's Xpress
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and the pace-maker for every scenario; has struggled to convert recent 5f form into wins (0W from 15 similar-going starts) but a step up to 6f in a small-pace field may suit her stamina better than her sprinting figures suggest.

runners_data.name: Von Krolock
runners_data.note: In excellent current form with a recent win and a second on Good and Standard, and his last two 6f runs have been competitive; the hood (headgear) is retained, and the 12-day turnaround under an in-form trainer (T14: 3/42) makes him a live prominent player.

runners_data.name: Methgal
runners_data.note: Won over today's 6f trip on Good ground recently and the tongue-tie is familiar equipment; trainer Dylan Cunha has been active (5/21 in 14 days) and Kyle McHugh's 7lb claim brings the weight down meaningfully, making this a legitimate stakes player tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Insuspense
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a strong placed record (0W3P from similar-going starts) who has finished second three times on Soft/Standard — the Good ground today is slightly quicker than ideal, and 86 days off is a significant absence flag; the tongue-tie is retained.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose single Good-ground run in this sample returned only 1 place from 15, and a modest pace set by Sam's Xpress gives little chance of a late surge; Jack Mitchell is a strong jockey booking but the race shape makes this a difficult assignment for a closer.

runners_data.name: Danger Alert
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on a horse that is a genuine rear-of-field type by nature, though with hold-up runners compressed, he is likely to race closer than his preferred position; 99 days since last run is a concern, and the equine shield/eye-shield headgear is new — his style fit in this shape is reduced (0.91).

runners_data.name: Deadline
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a limited form book (four runs, all 4th-6th) who has not yet shown the ability to convert close proximity into a win; 6f on Good at Yarmouth is within scope but the youth and form suggest raw upside rather than immediate winning likelihood.

runners_data.name: Woolridge
runners_data.note: A horse whose natural home is at the back of the field — with several rivals pushing toward the same rear positions, he is squeezed into a midfield mapping that is not his preference (style fit 0.91); Scott Dixon's team have had a quiet 14 days (0/24) and the pace scenario does not set up for him.

runners_data.name: My Mate Kev
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is an eye-catching booking for a horse that has shown ability when placed, including a win on Standard and two places — but he is a true hold-up type redistributed forward in this map (style fit 0.92), and the modest pace of this race asks him to come from too far back on a flat straight track.

runners_data.name: Kyoto
runners_data.note: Has a steady record of placed finishes on slower surfaces but yet to win; the 81-day break is a notable absence concern, and as a natural hold-up runner compressed into a midfield slot (style fit 0.90), the controlled pace Sam's Xpress will set offers minimal late-race acceleration for him to exploit.

races.paceDynamic: Sam's Xpress is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap at Yarmouth on Good ground, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Noble Guest and Von Krolock will press forward into prominent positions just off Sam's Xpress, creating a compact early formation rather than a high-octane sprint, which tilts the advantage firmly toward horses who can race close to the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a late burst. Yarmouth's straight 6f track offers no hiding place and rewards those who travel smoothly in the first half of the race, meaning prominent racers who save energy behind a moderate single pace-setter are best placed. This race shape unequivocally favours prominent-to-midfield types who can sit two to three lengths off Sam's Xpress, travel comfortably, and kick at the two-furlong pole — the true hold-up contingent is large and several cannot get their natural position. Danger Alert, Woolridge, My Mate Kev, and Kyoto are all genuine rear-of-field horses redistributed into the midfield on the map because there are simply too many hold-up types for the pace on offer; of these, Danger Alert with Pat Cosgrave and My Mate Kev with Silvestre De Sousa are most likely to push for a forward position in practice, though even they face a compromised trip against a modest solo pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sam's Xpress Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Xpress sets an uncontested, even tempo and the hold-up horses are held up too far back to land a telling blow.
scenarios.body: Sam's Xpress controls the race from the front without pressure, and the prominent pair of Von Krolock and Methgal track her at their own pace before quickening through the final furlong; Yarmouth's flat, straight 6f suits those who travel close to a manageable solo pace and strike at the right moment.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Xpress ties herself up slightly in the final furlong after setting the pace, allowing the prominent stalkers to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Noble Guest and Von Krolock, racing just off the pace throughout, inherit the lead as Sam's Xpress weakens inside the final furlong; both have recent course-distance form on Good ground to recommend them, and their positioning gives them first run on the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and opens a gap for a horse finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Court Drive, Insuspense, or Deadline would need a strong late surge, but the modest pace set by a single front-runner makes such a finish improbable; any closer who does land a blow will need to have tracked closer than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Pace Plan
scenarios.trigger: If Sam's Xpress misses the break or races ungenerously, causing the pace to collapse and creating a false-pace scenario.
scenarios.body: Without Sam's Xpress establishing early rhythm, several horses attempt to claim the lead mid-pack, creating a muddling tempo that can produce an unexpected winner from a wide-margin hold-up run; Danger Alert's bigger-field experience gives her a small edge in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Sam's Xpress must break cleanly and stride on immediately — if she misses the kick or shows any reluctance, the entire race shape collapses with no obvious pace replacement, creating chaos that scrambles all scenario probabilities.

Von Krolock's hood and recent course-form combination makes him the chief prominent threat to watch tracking the pace — if he travels smoothly in second or third place through the first three furlongs, he is well-positioned to strike.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Danger Alert, My Mate Kev, Woolridge, Kyoto) will all be bidding for similar real estate in the rear half of the field — watch for crowding and interference in the early stages as riders compete for position.

Methgal's tongue-tie and 6f Good-ground win are the stand-out form credentials among the prominent pack; if Kyle McHugh (7lb claim) positions him correctly off Sam's Xpress's shoulder, his recent sharp form makes him a pace shape beneficiary worth monitoring.

Court Drive and Insuspense are the hold-up horses with the best form credentials but face the same structural problem — a lone, manageable front-runner on a straight 6f gives closers almost no realistic opportunity to generate a finishing burst powerful enough to overhaul those racing prominently.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Commercial Fit-out Challenge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up galloper who showed good-ground form winning at 6f and placed at 7f — the 7f trip on today's surface suits, and Harry Davies provides useful conditional weight relief, though he needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Cuban Girl
runners_data.note: Natural closer dropped back from 10f trips and struggling on Southwell's synthetic — the return to good turf is a positive but she is carrying 135lbs and needs more pace than Oh So Perfect is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Gemini Star
runners_data.note: Has placed at 6f on good ground but her best form has come over shorter distances and on Southwell's AW; Dylan Hogan's booking is interesting but her hold-up style is a handicap in a race where pace is pedestrian.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: David Simcock's consistent performer with two wins and multiple places on good ground over 7f-8f — races from the rear by instinct but has the engine to close from a handy position, and Daniel Muscutt is a significant booking in this company.

runners_data.name: Pickering Castle
runners_data.note: Has failed to win in 13 starts on good going and all five recent runs have been on Southwell's standard surface; a true hold-up horse whose style is already a mismatch for today's moderate pace, and the ground switch does not resolve his form concerns.

runners_data.name: Potters Prince
runners_data.note: Absent 141 days and returning from a break without a prep run; naturally races from behind and with 0 wins from 6 starts on good ground, the conditions do not compensate for the fitness question and the mismatch in race shape.

runners_data.name: Court Of Session
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good ground wearing a visor and has experience at this trip, but his record of 1 place from 15 good-ground starts tells a clear story; he needs a sharper surface and a stronger pace than today's shape will provide.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Three wins at 8f on good ground is an excellent profile, but he is dropping to 7f today and is a genuine hold-up type shuffled toward midfield by a crowded rear — his form is strong enough to matter if the pace quickens.

runners_data.name: Oh So Perfect
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and set to have it entirely her own way; Michael Appleby's three-year-old has won twice on Southwell's standard surface and mason Paetel rides with a 3lb claim, though note all her career wins have come at Southwell rather than on turf.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is the headline here, and Yoko placed at 6f on good ground last time out — but her true colours are hold-up and she has no wins from six good-ground starts, leaving her vulnerable in a shape that gives little late reward.

runners_data.name: Captive Beauty
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — that tendency combined with being pushed out of her natural rearward position makes her a hard horse to back; the Josephine Gordon booking adds interest but does not solve the tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Withoutfurtherado
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist whose best efforts have come over 10f on good ground — dropping to 7f today asks a question of his stamina in reverse and his style means he will be last off the bridle in a race that will already be won up front.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground at this course, which is a major positive flag; Grace McEntee's claim helps with the weight, and while she races from behind by nature, her Yarmouth course form over today's exact trip marks her as the most interesting of the hold-up contingent.

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and visor and ran just four days ago — that quick turnaround combined with 0 wins from nine good-ground starts and a hold-up style in a slow-run race makes it very difficult to see a winning scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Perfect is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press from the gate, she is set to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo around Yarmouth's flat, sweeping 7f track. That uncontested lead on good ground is a significant tactical asset — she can conserve energy through the first half of the race and still have petrol left when the field closes beneath her in the final quarter-mile. The vast majority of this field are true hold-up horses shuffled into the middle of the pack by necessity, not preference; Yoko, Captive Beauty, Potters Prince, Withoutfurtherado, Caitlin G and several others are natural come-from-behind types who are genuinely redistributed and will race wide of their comfort zone at the sharp end. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and any horse comfortable racing prominently in behind — a steady honest gallop set by one horse suits those who can latch on early rather than those who need a truly fast pace to generate momentum from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Perfect dictates an uncontested moderate pace and none of the redistributed hold-up horses can bridge the gap late.
scenarios.body: Oh So Perfect holds every card up front, sets fractions to suit herself on good ground, and simply kicks clear when the pressure finally comes two furlongs out; the lack of genuine pace competition means she is never put under early stress.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned just behind Oh So Perfect tracks her through and times a run to reel her in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows a well-positioned trailer to get a perfect tow and produce a powerful finishing effort with the leader caught flat-footed; Campani, with his strong good-ground form and tactical versatility, is the prototype beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Suits Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Perfect quickens the tempo sooner than expected and the pace becomes strong enough to open the race up for a late closer.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated early pace would string the field out and create a genuine stamina test over the 7f trip, giving the handful of authentic hold-up horses — Giant and Desert Charm in particular — a chance to motor through beaten rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Perfect fades sharply in the final furlong after dictating alone, creating a messy blanket finish among the trailing pack.
scenarios.body: Without a dominant winner up front, the contest dissolves into a sprint from two furlongs out and any horse who has been conserving energy just off the pace can benefit from the vacuum; Caitlin G, with her win from behind at this course, is one who could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Perfect has all her career wins on Southwell's all-weather, not turf — watch whether Mason Paetel (3lb claim) can adapt her front-running style to good turf at Yarmouth, as any signs of greenness or traffic issues early could unravel the entire race shape.

Campani's trainer David Simcock also saddles Pickering Castle, giving the yard two runners — watch the market to identify which of the pair the stable is more bullish about, as Campani's good-ground form and Daniel Muscutt's booking suggest he may be the yard's primary hope.

Caitlin G's win over 7f on this exact course on good going is a live form pointer in a field where most rivals lack Yarmouth turf course experience — watch if she drifts or firms in the market, as she is the most interesting hold-up horse in the race.

Desert Charm has three wins on good ground but all over 8f — the drop to 7f on a flat, straight track means he may find the race over before he gets going; watch where Kieran O'Neill positions him in the early stages as a clue to connections' confidence.

With 13 of 14 runners classified as hold-up types and most of them redistributed by necessity, watch for any horse that breaks unexpectedly forward from the gate — any runner breaching Oh So Perfect's space early could transform the pace and trigger Scenario C or D.

races.name: Gold & Silver Exchange Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Symphony Of Joy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Frost yard that finds this 1m trip on good ground within her comfort zone, though her recent form string of 70634 shows no win and limited placed efforts at this trip in similar conditions; true last-to-first style means she needs a stronger gallop than Amarachi is likely to supply.

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Sangster's three-year-old arrives in decent form having won last time at Sandown and shown placed effort over 8f on good ground; Jack Callan rides for a yard operating at a strong 13% 14-day strike rate, and a horse that finished second over 8f on good gives genuine confidence it can travel prominently enough to benefit from a muddling pace.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on good ground for John Ryan — the most relevant recent form in the race — and handles this going well across 13 runs on similar surfaces; his true running style is deep hold-up, but with so many rivals also wanting the same ground at the rear, he may race closer than usual, which could suit if the pace is genuinely steady.

runners_data.name: Captain Corelli
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from 283 days off for Julie Camacho, which is an immediate concern regardless of the booking; his form on good going spans five placed efforts over 8f but the layoff and age make it hard to trust at a competitive price, and his natural last-off-the-pace style will be compromised if the field fails to string out.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse showing 239325 in recent form, with four placed finishes from eight runs on similar going and a hood fitted to sharpen focus; Liam Wright takes the ride for a trainer with just one runner in the past 14 days, and his tendency to race as a true hold-up type may see him pushed forward in a race lacking pace, which the form suggests he can handle at this trip.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Two consecutive third-place finishes over this exact 8f trip on good ground give Ashley Lewis a live each-way chance on form, and the horse handles the surface well across six qualifying runs; naturally a deep hold-up type, the redistribution towards midfield is realistic given how many closers contest this race, and a clear run from that position is his best-case scenario.

runners_data.name: Meritocratic
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old has been off 70 days and steps back from the 10f trips that dominated recent outings to try a mile; Mason Paetel's booking for a trainer firing at 7% over 42 runners in the past fortnight is not encouraging, and the horse's placed effort at 10f suggests the shorter trip may not fully play to its stamina profile.

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's four-year-old has two seconds on good-ish ground and is mapped to the front as the likeliest pace-setter, though its natural preference appears to be for a more prominent rather than dictating role; Connor Planas must decide early whether to commit to the lead or drift back, and at OR 53 — the lowest in the field — it carries least weight, which could make that front position surprisingly durable if the pace is sensibly managed.

races.paceDynamic: Amarachi is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this race, redistributed to the front having shown prominent tendencies, and will almost certainly dictate from the outset at a measured, uncontested gallop over Yarmouth's flat mile. With no genuine front-runner to apply pressure, the tempo is likely to be steady early, creating a falsely run race where position and tactical acumen matter more than raw stamina. The bulk of the field — Crimson Rambler, Ecclefechan, Meritocratic, Captain Corelli, Big Alex Walmsley, Piazza and Symphony Of Joy — are all true hold-up types, but so many cannot realistically settle at the rear simultaneously; those with the lowest draw or most assertive riders will drift closer than their natural style suggests. A slowly-run mile with one honest front-runner and a compressed midfield suits a horse that can travel prominently or make a forward move off the final bend, giving a decisive advantage to any runner able to secure a handy position and quicken from two furlongs out rather than a true deep closer arriving from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amarachi Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Amarachi dictates a steady, uncontested pace and kicks on turning for home before the field can organise.
scenarios.body: Amarachi sets an uncontested tempo with no rival willing to go with him, meaning the field dawdles in a bunch and the race becomes a sprint from two out; horses that travel close to the pace or secure a handy pitch benefit enormously because there is simply no searching gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Compressed Field Sprints Home
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace bunches the field so tightly that a late-charging hold-up horse finds room and pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race with a wall of horses simultaneously producing their effort from two furlongs out creates a lottery finish; the horse with the sharpest turn of foot and a clear passage benefits, while those shuffled wide or trapped on the rail lose ground at the crucial moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield types surges earlier than expected to challenge Amarachi, lifting the tempo from the half-mile pole.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop from halfway stretches the field and rewards genuine stamina over a flat mile rather than pure finishing speed; horses that handle a true end-to-end test and have shown form over this trip and trip on good ground come into their own.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Amarachi Wilts Late
scenarios.trigger: If Amarachi's early lead proves unsustainable in the final two furlongs and a deep hold-up horse finds an unobstructed run.
scenarios.body: A front-runner that has set even a moderate pace can still tire on a flat track if racing out of natural role; a genuine hold-up horse that has found clear air late and covers ground efficiently could scoop up the stragglers, though this scenario is undermined by the fact that most closers here are also out of role.

watchPoints.text: Piazza's Callan has a yard firing at a strong recent strike rate and the horse's winning form over 8f on good ground makes it the most dangerous if it secures a handy pitch off a slow pace — watch for it to travel prominently and kick clear inside the final two furlongs.

Amarachi's rider Connor Planas will need to commit to the front role immediately from the gate — any hesitation and the pace collapses entirely, potentially turning the race into a sprint that benefits every horse except the notional leader.

Captain Corelli returns from a 283-day absence and is nine years old; if he shows signs of rustiness in the early stages or is outpaced as the field bunches, he risks being a significant drifter in running at short odds — watch his early market move as a gauge of stable confidence.

With six genuine hold-up types trying to occupy the rear of the field simultaneously, watch which horses are forced to race wider or closer than their jockeys intend in the first two furlongs — those trapped in traffic on the inside of a bunched field face the greatest risk of a poor run.

Ecclefechan's winning run came just six days ago and a quick turnaround on good ground at Yarmouth is worth monitoring in the paddock for signs of freshness or fatigue before assessing his market position.
